rules.title: Anti-Eviction Statute
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict only on the statutory grounds, such as nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, health and safety violations, permanent retirement of the property, condominium conversion, owner occupancy and certain criminal offenses. Each ground carries its own Notice to Quit period, ranging from 3 days to 3 years. Relocation assistance is required for some grounds.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit from 3 days up to 3 years depending on the ground; 18 months for permanent retirement from residential use; 3 years for condominium conversion; relocation assistance of six times monthly rent for illegal occupancy
rules.penalty: Self-help eviction or lockout is illegal and the landlord may be liable for damages, court costs and attorney fees. Unpaid relocation amounts accrue 18% annual interest and become a lien on the property.
rules.status_basis: Statute is in the code and is described as the Anti-Eviction Statute.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental tenancies in New Jersey, including owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings, which have a reduced list of grounds.

rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
